relearning.title: Read: distance, time and speed
relearning.description: A short reading with the road-trip analogy, worked examples and quick checks.

body.text:
**I can define and calculate distance, time and speed.**

**Think of a road trip on Highway 29.** The odometer tells you how far you went (distance). The clock tells you how long it took (time). The speedometer tells you how fast you are going right now (speed). If you know any two of these, you can figure out the third.

**Distance** is how far an object has traveled, measured in meters (m). **Speed** is the distance an object travels per unit of time, so a speed unit is always a distance unit over a time unit: m/s, km/h, mph, mi/min.

**The speed triangle:** d on top, s and t on the bottom. Cover what you want. **Speed = Distance/Time** (S = d/t). **Distance = speed × time** (d = s × t). **Time = Distance/Speed** (t = d/s). Every answer needs **Formula / Set Up / Answer with units.**

**Worked example:** A runner goes 150 m in 20 s. What is the runner's speed? Formula: S = d/t. Set Up: S = 150 m / 20 s. Answer: **7.5 m/s**.

checks.prompt: A student walks 90 m in 60 s. Which setup finds the speed?
checks.explanation: Speed = distance / time, so distance goes on top: 90 m / 60 s = 1.5 m/s. Multiplying, or putting time on top, is the common mistake.

checks.prompt: A car drives at 25 m/s for 8 s. How many meters does it travel? Type a number.
checks.explanation: You know speed and time, so use d = s × t: 25 m/s × 8 s = 200 m. Dividing (25 ÷ 8) is the common mistake. Cover d in the triangle: s and t sit side by side, which means multiply.

sections.title: Average speed and displacement

body.text:
**More speed words.** **Average speed** = total distance / total time for the whole trip. **Instantaneous speed** is the speed at one moment, like a speedometer shows. **Constant speed** means equal distances in equal times; **changing speed** means speeding up or slowing down. **Displacement** is the distance and direction from the starting point. Walk 50 m north, then 30 m south: distance = 80 m, but displacement = 20 m north.

**Worked example 2:** A family drives 30 miles at 40 mph. How many minutes does it take? (1 hour = 60 minutes) Formula: t = d/s. Set Up: t = 30 mi / 40 mi/h = 0.75 h. Convert: 0.75 h × 60 = **45 minutes**.

**Worked example 3:** A group of bikers ride 90 km in the first 2 hours and 30 km in the last 1 hour. What is their average speed? Formula: average speed = total distance / total time. Set Up: (90 km + 30 km) / (2 h + 1 h) = 120 km / 3 h. Answer: **40 km/h**. Averaging the two speeds (45 km/h and 30 km/h) gives 37.5 km/h, which is wrong.

**Watch out for:** using the wrong form of the triangle (multiplying when you should divide), leaving off units, mixing minutes and hours (convert first when the answer is in mph or km/h), averaging speeds instead of using total distance ÷ total time, and mixing up distance with displacement.

checks.prompt: A student walks 70 m east, then turns around and walks 30 m west. What are the distance and the displacement?
checks.explanation: Distance counts every meter: 70 m + 30 m = 100 m. Displacement is measured from the starting point, and opposite directions subtract: 70 m − 30 m = 40 m east. Mixing up the two is the common mistake.

checks.prompt: A student walks 300 m in 150 s, then runs 300 m in 50 s. What is the average speed for the whole trip, in m/s? Type a number.
checks.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time = (300 m + 300 m) / (150 s + 50 s) = 600 m / 200 s = 3 m/s. Averaging the two speeds (2 m/s and 6 m/s) gives 4 m/s, which is the common mistake.

sections.shortAnswer: Explain the difference between distance and displacement using a trip from your house to school and back.

relearning.title: Do: solve speed problems step by step
relearning.description: Two worked problems shown one step at a time: finding speed, then a trip with a turnaround.

body.problem: A cyclist rides 1,800 m on a trail in 300 s. What is the cyclist's speed?

steps.text: List what you know: distance d = 1,800 m and time t = 300 s. You want the speed.
Formula: cover S in the speed triangle. That leaves d over t, so S = d/t.
Set Up: S = 1,800 m / 300 s. Distance goes on top, time on the bottom.
Answer with units: S = 6 m/s. Meters over seconds gives m/s.

checks.prompt: Your turn: you know a speed and a time, and you want the distance. Which formula do you use?
checks.explanation: Cover d in the triangle: s and t sit side by side, which means multiply, so d = s × t. Dividing is the common mistake.

checks.prompt: Your turn: a tarantula crawls 3 m in 6 s. What is its speed in m/s? Type a number.
checks.explanation: S = d/t = 3 m / 6 s = 0.5 m/s. Dividing 6 by 3 (getting 2) is the common mistake: distance goes on top.

sections.title: Worked problem: a trip with a turnaround

body.problem: A student walks 120 m east in 60 s, then turns around and walks 40 m west in 20 s. Find the distance, the displacement and the average speed.

steps.text: Distance counts every meter, no matter the direction: 120 m + 40 m = 160 m.
Displacement is the distance and direction from the start. The student walked back toward the start, so subtract: 120 m − 40 m = 80 m east.
Average speed = total distance / total time = 160 m / 80 s = 2 m/s. Use the distance (160 m), not the displacement (80 m).

checks.prompt: Your turn: a jogger runs 90 m north, then turns around and runs 25 m south. What is the jogger's displacement?
checks.explanation: Opposite directions subtract: 90 m − 25 m = 65 m, and the jogger is still north of the start. 115 m is the distance, not the displacement, which is the common mistake.

checks.prompt: Your turn: a student walks 300 m to a friend's house in 250 s, then walks straight back in 150 s. What is the average speed for the whole trip, in m/s? Type a number.
checks.explanation: Average speed uses the total distance: 300 m + 300 m = 600 m, over the total time: 250 s + 150 s = 400 s. 600 m / 400 s = 1.5 m/s. Using the displacement (0 m, since the trip ends where it started) is the common mistake.

checks.prompt: A cyclist rides 600 m in 120 s. What is her speed?
checks.explanation: Formula: S = d/t. Set Up: S = 600 m / 120 s. Answer: 5 m/s. Multiplying (72,000) or dividing time by distance (0.2) uses the wrong form of the triangle, and a speed unit is always distance over time, not just m.

checks.prompt: A dog runs 48 m at a speed of 8 m/s. How many seconds does it take? Type a number.
checks.explanation: Cover t on the speed triangle: t = d/s. Set Up: t = 48 m / 8 m/s. Answer: 6 s.

sections.title: Average speed

checks.prompt: A car drives 120 km in the first 2 h and 30 km in the next 1 h. What is its average speed for the whole trip?
checks.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time. Set Up: (120 km + 30 km) / (2 h + 1 h) = 150 km / 3 h. Answer: 50 km/h. Averaging the two speeds (60 and 30 km/h gives 45 km/h) is the common mistake.

checks.prompt: A speedometer reads 45 mph at one moment during a trip. What does that number show?

options.text: The average speed for the trip

checks.explanation: A speedometer shows the speed at one moment, which is the instantaneous speed. Average speed is total distance / total time for the whole trip.

sections.shortAnswer: A family drives 100 miles in 2 hours, with a stop for lunch. Explain why their average speed is 50 mph even though the speedometer did not always read 50.
